key_expressions: When should we have our team meeting?,
Are you okay with the role division?,
We should start preparing the presentation,

A: When would be a good time for our team meeting this week?
I’m free tomorrow afternoon, but I’m not sure if everyone else is.
If another time works better, please let me know.
B: Tomorrow afternoon works for me as well.
I think the other members can probably make that time too.
Why don’t we post it in the group chat and confirm?

A: How should we divide the roles for this project?
I’m comfortable organizing things or preparing the slides.
Is there a part you’d prefer to take?
B: That sounds great — having someone strong in organization really helps.
I’m more comfortable with research and analysis.
If we choose tasks that suit our strengths, we’ll work much more efficiently.

A: How far have we gotten with gathering sources?
I already collected a few related papers.
I can share them right away if you need them.
B: Oh, you’ve found that many already? Thanks a lot!
I’ve been looking mainly at statistical data.
If we combine our materials, the project will be much stronger.

A: Our shared folder feels a bit messy right now.
Should I reorganize it and set up a clearer structure?
I can also rename the files so they’re easier to identify.
B: That would help us so much, thank you.
It’s been difficult to find things because everything is scattered.
If you organize it, it’ll make our work much smoother.

A: When should we start preparing for the presentation?
I think starting midweek would be manageable.
Should I draft a basic slide layout first?
B: Yes, that timing sounds good.
If you make a layout first, it’ll be easier for us to add our parts.
A simple draft is more than enough to get us going.

A: Did you already summarize the points from today’s meeting?
I only wrote down a few things, so mine feels incomplete.
If you organized anything, could you share it?
B: Yes, I summarized everything right after the meeting.
I kept it short and focused on the key decisions.
I’ll upload it to the group chat now so everyone can check it.

A: I noticed there are quite a lot of evaluation criteria for this project.
The presentation score looks higher than I expected, so I’m a bit worried.
Maybe we should practice our presentation a few times.
B: I thought the same — the presentation has a big weight.
But if we practice ahead of time, we’ll be fine.
How about doing two or three rehearsals together?

A: It seems like each team is progressing at a different pace.
Maybe we should break our timeline into smaller steps too.
Should we start by setting this week’s goals?
B: That’s a great idea. Having clear goals really helps us stay on track.
Let’s outline the key tasks we need to finish this week.
I already have a shortlist, so I can share it with you.

A: Should we also set aside some time to review each other’s parts?
A bit of feedback from everyone could improve the final quality.
Would meeting sometime this weekend work?
B: Yes, having a review session would be very helpful.
I’m available both in the morning and afternoon this weekend.
Just tell me what time works for you, and I’ll adjust.

A: We’re finally getting close to finishing this project!
I’m glad everything went smoothly thanks to the teamwork.
As long as we wrap things up carefully, the submission should be fine.
B: I agree — our teamwork really made the process easier.
Let’s just double-check everything before we submit.
A quick final review together will make sure it's all solid.
